# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.

# Research Report: Transaction Categorization & Payee Extraction

## 1) Overall repo structure

```
/app
├── .gitignore
├── Dockerfile                       # python:3.9.2, runs gunicorn on port 9898
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                     # Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, numpy/scipy/sklearn
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py              # Flask app factory (app = Flask(...)), imports Controller
        ├── Controller.py            # 936 lines. Flask routes; per-bank orchestration pipeline
        ├── BankScripts/             # 35 bank-specific rule engines (one file per Indian bank)
        │   ├── HDFC.py, ICICI.py, SBI.py, IDBI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, PNB.py,
        │   ├── YES.py, IDFC.py, BOB.py, BOI.py, Canara.py, Federal.py, RBL.py,
        │   ├── UnionBank.py, UCO.py, Citi.py, Paytm.py, StandardCharted.py,
        │   └── ... (Andhra, AuSmallFinanceBank, Bandhan, BankOfMaharashtra, Central,
        │        CityUnion, DCB, Indian, Indusind, Karnataka, KarurVyasa, Saraswat,
        │        SouthIndian, SVC, Syndicate, TamilnadMerchantile)
        └── UtilityScripts/
            ├── AppUtil.py                    # tokenizer/extractor helpers (sep_by_*, py_extract)
            ├── RegexConstants.py             # cross-bank regex constants
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py         # 432 lines of per-bank regex constants
            ├── CleanName.py                  # 1971 lines: partyName normalization / extraction
            ├── CardCleanNames.py             # same, for credit-card statements
            ├── Purpose.py / CardPurpose.py   # purpose tagging (LOAN, RENT_INCOME, ...)
            ├── PFMCategorization.py          # PFM category mapping (incl. REVERSAL bucket)
            ├── SimpleDescription.py          # human-readable description from category
            ├── InternalPayment.py            # self-transfer detection (fuzzy match on holder)
            ├── SalaryDetection.py            # salary heuristics
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py              # recurring transaction detection
            ├── TransactionCategoryEnums.py   # category display names (Cheque, NACH, Reversal...)
            └── TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

This is a Flask microservice ("transaction-enrichment-python"). Everything is pandas/numpy rule engines: lists of `[boolean-Series condition, choice]` pairs fed to `np.select`, ordered by priority.

## 2) Where classification and name extraction happen

### Orchestration
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`
  - `categorizeTransaction()` route, line 69–70. For each bank it runs the same pipeline: `categorize_<Bank>_transactions()` → `card_clean_names`/`card_purpose` (credit cards) → `purpose()` → `clean_names()` → `internal_payment()` → `salary_detection()` → `pfm_categorization()` → `simple_description()`. (Repeated per bank; e.g., HDFC branch lines 163–186, IDBI branch lines 235–258.)
  - `recurrentTransactions()` route, line 55–56.

### Transaction-type classification (cheque, transfer, refund, reversal, mandate verification, etc.)
Each `BankScripts/<Bank>.py` file defines `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` (always at line 8–9) whose **first `conditions_choices` block assigns `transactionCategory`** via `np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")`. Representative examples:

- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`
  - Category rules: lines 11–104. Refund lines 19–20; card reversal (`CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`) line 21; UPI/IMPS reversal lines 22–23; generic REVERSAL line 25; cheque rules (`CHEQUE_PAID`/`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`/`CHEQUE_RETURN`/`CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL`) lines 50, 69–75, 100; account (penny-drop/mandate) verification line 13; NEFT/RTGS/UPI/IMPS/TPT lines 57–61; default `TRANSFER` line 104.
  - Subcategory rules: lines 112–132 (e.g., `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE` line 126).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py` — category rules lines 10–62: cheque return line 25, refund line 26, ACH/NACH auto-payment line 38, cheque paid/deposit lines 55–58.
- Mandate verification / mandate charges rules (examples): `Axis.py:24–28` (`MANDATE` + amount 1 → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`; `MNDTVRFCHGS` → `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES`), `Indusind.py:29–33`, `PNB.py:12–14`, `SBI.py:33`, `Syndicate.py:34` (`MANDATE VER CHG|MNDT:VR:CHG`), `Canara.py:44`, `BOI.py:21`, `Federal.py:21`, `UnionBank.py:30`.
- Category vocabularies: `UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` (e.g., `CHEQUE_COLLECTION` line 9, `ECS/NACH` line 34, `NACH` line 37, `REVERSAL` line 62, `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` line 94) and `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py`.
- Shared regex constants: `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` — HDFC cheque patterns `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10` lines 81–90; PNB cheque patterns lines 140–148; Kotak fund-transfer/cheque patterns `FT_CHQ_PATTERN1..37` lines 263–299 and `CHQ_PATTERN1..4` lines 314–318; reversal constants per bank lines 323–412 (`REVERSAL_CANARA`, `REVERSAL_KV`, `REVERSAL_YES`, ...); account-verification constant `BANK_VER_HD` line 75. Also `UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` (e.g., `BANK_LOAN_CHQ` line 18).

### Payee / counterparty name extraction from narration
Done in **two layers**:

Layer 1 — inside each bank script, a later `conditions_choices` block assigns `transactions['partyName']` using positional token splits and regex extraction:
- Helpers in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`: `sep_by_` (split on `/`) line 14, `sep_by_dash` line 17, plus `sep_by_wave/star/comma/colon/under/brckt...` lines 20–45, and regex extractor `py_extract()` lines 61–66; `fuzzy_match()` line 48.
- Your exact examples:
  - **"ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES"** → `IDBI.py` lines 81–86: `"^ACH-BD-NACH"` and `"^ACH-BD-"` → `sep_by_dash(description, 2, 3)`; also `"\\bETPC.*ACH-BD-"` line 81, `"^ACH-BARB-"` line 85, `"^ACH-"` line 86. HDFC equivalent: `HDFC.py` lines 169–174 (`"^ACH D- BD-NACH-"` → `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)` with digit stripping). PNB equivalent: `PNB.py:143` (`^ACH/|NACH-DR/` → `sep_by_(...,1,2)`).
  - **"GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR"** (bank-code + long ref + name) → `IDBI.py` line 110: matches `"^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}"` and extracts via `py_extract(pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)")`. Similar UTR-style extraction in `StandardCharted.py` lines 90, 92, 159 (`CASH [A-Z]{5}[0-9]+ (.*) (RTGS|SENDER)`).
  - **Cheque numbers/narrations** → `IDBI.py` lines 80, 104, 107–109 (`^CHQ Paid/`, `/CHQ DEP/`, 6-digit cheque numbers); `HDFC.py` line 163 (`CHQ PAID-` → `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)`); Kotak/PNB cheque-name patterns in `BankRegexConstants.py` (lines 81–90, 140–148, 263–318 incl. `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK` line 318 which strips bank names from cheque payee strings).
  - Cleanup passes: `IDBI.py` lines 119–126 (fixes `Na`, single letters, numeric-only names), line 116 (`str.title().str.strip()`), line 128 creates `party2` (whitespace-stripped variant).
- `IDBI.py` also derives `city` from card narrations (lines 142–245).

Layer 2 — global normalization:
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py`, `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` at line 9 (1,971 lines). Maps raw partyName/description fragments to canonical merchant/biller names (DTH, broadband, electricity, lenders, etc.), including NACH loan patterns, e.g., line 602 (`NACH- DR/EQUITAS` → "Equitas Bank Loan ..."), lines 1745–1756 (`^EMI [0-9]+ CHQ` / `^NACH-DR/HDFC BANK LIMITED/0` → "HDFC Bank Loan ...").
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py`, `card_clean_names()` line 9 (credit cards).
- Downstream consumers of category+partyName: `Purpose.py` `purpose()` line 9, `CardPurpose.py` line 9, `PFMCategorization.py` `pfm_categorization()` line 8 (line 73 folds REVERSAL/REFUND/RETURN/BOUNCE into a PFM "REVERSAL" bucket), `SimpleDescription.py` line 6, `InternalPayment.py` `internal_payment()` line 8, `SalaryDetection.py` `salary_detection()` line 16.

## 3) Test files covering this logic

**There are none.** I searched exhaustively:
- No `tests/` directory, no `test_*.py`/`*_test*` files anywhere (`glob **/*test*` returns nothing; the repo contains only the 52 source files listed above).
- No pytest/tox/nose config (`pytest.ini`, `setup.cfg`, `pyproject.toml`, `conftest.py` all absent), no CI workflows.
- `setup.py` declares no test dependencies. The only test-related artifact is a `.gitignore` entry for `TEST*.xml` (unit-test report pattern from the gitignore template) — nothing is committed.
- Git history is a single commit (`fc21c7f import codebase`), so no tests were ever removed.

## 4) How to run tests

There is nothing to run — `pytest` (installed in this environment, v9.1.1) would collect 0 tests. The only ways to exercise the logic are:

1. **Run the service and POST transactions** (the intended usage, per Dockerfile):
   ```bash
   cd /app/categorizationapp && pip install -e .
   gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
   # then:
   curl -X POST localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"bank":"HDFC","acc_type":"SAVING","accountUID":"x","accountHolder":"RAVI KUMAR","transactions":[{"description":"...","amount":"100","type":"DEBIT","balanceAfterTransaction":"0","remark":""}]}'
   ```
   (Or `docker build` using the provided Dockerfile.) Valid `bank` values are the strings in Controller.py, e.g., `HDFC`, `SBI`, `ICICI`, `IDBI`, `IDFC`, `PNB`, `KOTAK`, `AXIS`, `YES`, `UNION_BANK`, `PAYTM_BANK`, `STANDARD_CHARTERED`, etc.
2. **Call functions directly** in a Python shell — build a DataFrame with columns `description`, `amount`, `type` (`DEBIT`/`CREDIT`), `balanceAfterTransaction`, `remark`, then call e.g. `categorize_IDBI_transactions(df, "SAVING")` followed by `clean_names(df, "SAVING", "IDBI")` (note: `CleanName`/`Purpose` import the Flask `app` for logging, so import via the package).

Caveat: the pinned dependencies (Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4) are old; the code relies on legacy pandas/np.select behavior, so testing under the Dockerfile's python 3.9.2 + pinned deps is the safest path.

steps.message:
All five reported failures traced to five one-line defects in the deterministic rule engines. Fixes applied:

**1. Cheque filed as transfer** — `BankScripts/Indusind.py:64`
The remark-based cheque rule read `^[0-9]{5}$`, so a row whose note is exactly a 6-digit cheque number fell through to TRANSFER. Restored to `^[0-9]{5,6}$` (matching the identical rule in the sibling Axis script, lines 58–59). 5-digit remarks keep working.

**2. Salary payee shows "NACH"** — `BankScripts/IDBI.py:83`
For `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` the rule took dash-token 2 (`NACH`) instead of token 3 (the employer). Restored `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)` — consistent with HDFC's equivalent `^ACH D- BD-NACH-` rule, which uses tokens 3–4. Plain `^ACH-BD-` (3-part) narrations are untouched.

**3. Blank sender name on `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`** — `BankScripts/IDBI.py:110`
`py_extract(..., pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)` asked for capture group 1, but the pattern has only one group (index 0), so the extractor returned empty for every such row. Restored `index=0` (as used by the adjacent rules on lines 120–121).

**4. Mandate token charge filed as transfer** — `BankScripts/Axis.py:25`
The ₹2 mandate-confirmation rule had been changed to `amount.eq(1)`; the sibling IndusInd script carries the byte-identical rule with `amount.eq(2)` (Indusind.py:30). Restored `eq(2)`, so the nominal mandate charge is again ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION. ₹1 credits remain covered by the following rule.

**5. Card refund vs. card reversal depending on account type** — `BankScripts/Indusind.py:26`
The CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL rule compared `accountType == "SAVINGS"`, but the canonical value throughout the service is `"SAVING"` (Controller.py, all other scripts) — a dead condition, so every POS-credit ≥ 10 on a savings account fell to the REFUND rule below. Fixed the typo; small (<10) POS credits still map to REFUND, and CURRENT-account behavior is unchanged.

Verification (end-to-end through the Flask `/categorizeTransaction` pipeline):
- All five ticket narrations now produce the correct category/name (`Acme Industries`, `Ravi Kumar`, CHEQUE_PAID, ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION, CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL).
- A differential regression of 3,360 rows (48 narration shapes × all 35 banks × SAVING/CURRENT) against the pre-fix code shows only the intended rows changed; every ordinary UPI/IMPS/NEFT/POS/ATM/salary/charges/refund row is byte-identical. The only knock-on diff is the recovered `Ravi Kumar` name now correctly triggering the downstream INTERNAL_PAYMENT flag when it matches the account holder.
